title: Electrochemical Growth of Full Volume Meissner Effect Superconducting BKBO
authors: Oleksandr Foyevtsov, Kateryna Foyevtsova, Mohamed Oudah, Dan Bizzotto, George Sawatzky
abstract: In this work we show the results of electrochemical synthesis of BKBO crystals using three different experimental setup configurations. The setups differ between each other by varying level of control over physical variables and progressing from a two-electrode to a three-electrode configuration using highly oriented platinum counter electrode. By systematic analysis of the temperature dependence of the magnetic susceptibility at the superconducting transition of the collected crystals we observe that an order of magnitude sharper superconducting transition is achieved for the most comprehensive three-electrode setup. In addition, the level of chemical substitution can be controlled by the value of the overpotential versus reference electrode. We demonstrate that with this technique a full volume Meissner effect can be achieved with a sharp transition temperature for the superconducting crystal.
summary: This work details the electrochemical synthesis of superconducting BKBO crystals, demonstrating that upgrading from simple two-electrode setups to a precise three-electrode potentiostatic system is crucial. This advanced control allows researchers to achieve highly homogeneous crystals exhibiting a full volume Meissner effect and a sharp superconducting transition. The combination of magnetic and electrochemical diagnostics provides a powerful pathway for tuning superconducting properties.
main_problem: The primary goal was to synthesize high-quality, single-crystal superconducting $	ext{Ba}_{1-x}	ext{K}_x	ext{BiO}_3$ (BKBO) crystals exhibiting a full volume Meissner effect with a sharp superconducting transition.
main_result: Implementing a comprehensive three-electrode potentiostatic setup significantly improved crystal quality, leading to a markedly sharper superconducting transition and achieving a full Meissner response.
method: The study employed electrochemical synthesis (anodic electrocrystallization) and characterized the results using magnetic susceptibility measurements and in-situ Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS).
model_or_system: The physical system is the perovskite superconductor $	ext{Ba}_{1-x}	ext{K}_x	ext{BiO}_3$ (BKBO). The growth is controlled electrochemically, comparing basic two-electrode constant current methods against advanced three-electrode potentiostatic control.
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) across the superconducting transition, superconducting transition width, Meissner phase volume fraction, and EIS parameters ($R_{ct}$, $Q_{dl}$, CPE exponent).
important_parameters: Growth temperature ($225^\circ	ext{C}$), applied overpotential/voltage, and the control mechanism transitioning from two-electrode to three-electrode potentiostatic control.
main_assumptions: The interpretation of $T_c$ alone is insufficient to uniquely determine potassium content, and the EIS analysis assumes interface changes are slow enough for local measurements.
figures_summary: Figures compare magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) for different growth methods, showing the progressive sharpening of the transition. Other figures detail the electrochemical setups and the Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) used for EIS fitting.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares three electrochemical growth setups (Method 1, 2, and 3). It uses magnetic measurements to assess superconducting quality and employs in-situ EIS analysis to diagnose the underlying electrochemical processes governing nucleation and growth kinetics.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous application of electrochemical control (potentiostats, EIS) to tune material stoichiometry and crystal homogeneity mirrors techniques used in controlling interfaces in quantum devices.

Figure 5: Equivalent circuit model used to fit the EIS data: Rsoln – solution resistance; Qdl – constant phase element modeling the double layer capacitance; Rct – charge transfer resistance modelling the electrochemical crystal growth kinetics; W1 – Warburg impedance modelling the mass transport of the reactants; L1 – inductance modelling the non-ideal connectors and influence of the environment on the EIS measurement.
